spots.name: Frauenkirche, Dresden
spots.summary: The Frauenkirche is a Lutheran church in Dresden, the capital of the German state of Saxony. Destroyed during the Allied firebombing of Dresden towards the end of World War II, the church was reconstructed between 1994 and 2005.

spots.name: Zwinger
spots.summary: The baroque palace features a nympheum, many sculptures of Permoser, a bell pavilion and famous art collections. Do not miss the "Alte Meister" - you'll find Rafael's famous Sistine Madonna with its well-known angels there. Three separate exhibitions are housed in the Zwinger. (See below.) The Zwinger is part of the Dresden State Art Collections (SKD).

spots.name: Dresden Cathedral
spots.summary: Dresden Cathedral, or the Cathedral of the Holy Trinity, Dresden, previously the Catholic Church of the Royal Court of Saxony, called in German Katholische Hofkirche and since 1980 also known as Kathedrale Sanctissimae Trinitatis, is the Catholic Cathedral of Dresden.

spots.name: Dresden Castle

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dresden Castle or Royal Palace is one of the oldest buildings in Dresden, Germany. For almost 400 years, it was the residence of the electors (1547–1806) and kings (1806–1918) of Saxony from the Albertine House of Wettin as well as Kings of Poland (1697–1763).

spots.name: Green Vault
spots.summary: The Green Vault is a museum located in Dresden, Germany, which contains the largest treasure collection in Europe. The museum was founded in 1723 by Augustus the Strong of Poland and Saxony, and features a variety of exhibits in styles from Baroque to Classicism.

spots.name: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister
spots.summary: The Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister in Dresden, Germany, displays around 750 paintings from the 15th to the 18th centuries. It includes major Italian Renaissance works as well as Dutch and Flemish paintings. Outstanding works by German, French, and Spanish painters of the period are also among the gallery's attractions.

spots.name: Carola Bridge
spots.summary: The Carola Bridge was a road and tram bridge in Dresden, Germany, spanning the Elbe river. Originally built in 1895, it was destroyed by the SS on May 7, 1945 to slow the Soviet advance near the end of World War II. A replacement bridge was constructed between 1967 and 1971.

spots.name: Kreuzkirche
spots.summary: The Dresden Kreuzkirche is a Lutheran church in Dresden, Germany. It is the main church and seat of the Landesbischof of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of Saxony, and the largest church building in the Free State of Saxony. It also is home of the Dresdner Kreuzchor boys' choir.

spots.name: Brühl's Terrace
spots.summary: Brühl's Terrace is a historic architectural ensemble in Dresden, Germany. Nicknamed "The Balcony of Europe", the terrace stretches high above the bank of the river Elbe, and is located north of the recently rebuilt Neumarkt Square and the Frauenkirche.

spots.name: Yenidze
spots.summary: Yenidze is a former cigarette factory building in Dresden, Saxony, Germany built between 1907 and 1909. Today it is used as an office building. It is notable for its Moorish Revival exterior design which borrows design elements from mosques and the Alhambra in Spain.

spots.name: Semperoper
spots.summary: The Semperoper is the opera house of the Sächsische Staatsoper Dresden and the concert hall of the Staatskapelle Dresden. It is also home to the Semperoper Ballett. The building is located on the Theaterplatz near the Elbe River in the historic centre of Dresden, Germany.

spots.name: Loschwitz Bridge
spots.summary: Loschwitz Bridge is a cantilever truss bridge over the river Elbe in Dresden the capital of Saxony in Germany. It connects the city districts of Blasewitz and Loschwitz, two affluent residential areas, which around 1900 were amongst the most expensive in Europe.

spots.name: Augustus Bridge
spots.summary: The Augustus Bridge is a bridge in the city of Dresden, in the state Saxony in Germany.

spots.name: Neumarkt
spots.summary: The Neumarkt is a square and culturally significant section of central Dresden, Germany. The historic area was almost completely wiped out during the Allied bombing during the Second World War.

spots.name: Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden is a cultural institution in Dresden, Germany, owned by the State of Saxony. It is one of the most renowned and oldest museum institutions in the world, originating from the collections of the Saxon electors in the 16th century.

spots.name: Dresden Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Dresden Hauptbahnhof is the largest passenger station in the Saxon capital of Dresden. In 1898, it replaced the Böhmischen Bahnhof of the former Saxon-Bohemian State Railway, and was designed with its formal layout as the central station of the city.

spots.name: Albertinum
spots.summary: The Albertinum is a modern art museum. The sandstone-clad Renaissance Revival building is located on Brühl's Terrace in the historic center of Dresden, Germany. It is named after King Albert of Saxony.

spots.name: Theaterplatz
spots.summary: The Theaterplatz in Dresden is a historic square in the city. It is located in the west of the inner old town.

spots.name: Bundeswehr Military History Museum
spots.summary: The Bundeswehr Military History Museum is the military museum of the German Armed Forces, the Bundeswehr, and one of the major military history museums in Germany. It is located in a former military arsenal in the Albertstadt which is part of Dresden.

spots.name: Taschenbergpalais
spots.summary: The Hotel Taschenbergpalais Kempinski Dresden is a historic palace hotel managed by the Kempinski chain. It is located on Sophie Street, next to the Dresden Castle, in front of the Zwinger, and adjacent to the Semperoper and the Dresden Cathedral.

spots.name: Sophienkirche

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sophienkirche was a church in Dresden.

spots.name: Galerie Neue Meister
spots.summary: The Galerie Neue Meister in Dresden, Germany, displays around 300 paintings from the 19th century until today, including works from Otto Dix, Edgar Degas, Vincent van Gogh and Claude Monet. The gallery also exhibits a number of sculptures from the Dresden Sculpture Collection from the same period.

spots.name: Semper Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Semper Gallery or Semper Building in Dresden, Germany, was designed by the architect Gottfried Semper and constructed from 1847 until 1854.

spots.name: Kulturpalast
spots.summary: The Kulturpalast Dresden is a modernist building designed by Wolfgang Hänsch during the era of the German Democratic Republic. It was the largest multi-purpose hall in Dresden when it opened in 1969, and was used for concerts, dances, conferences and other events.

spots.name: Großer Garten
spots.summary: The Großer Garten is a Baroque style park in central Dresden. It is rectangular in shape and covers about 1.8 km2. Originally established in 1676 on the orders of John George III, Elector of Saxony, it has been a public garden since 1814. Pathways and avenues are arranged symmetrically throughout the park.

spots.name: Dresden Transport Museum
spots.summary: The Dresden Transport Museum displays vehicles of all modes of transport, such as railway, shipping, road and air traffic, under one roof.

spots.name: German Hygiene Museum
spots.summary: The German Hygiene Museum is a medical museum in Dresden, Germany. It conceives itself today as a "forum for science, culture and society". It is a popular venue for events and exhibitions, and is among the most visited museums in Dresden, with around 280,000 visitors per year.

spots.name: Dresden Suspension Railway
spots.summary: The Dresden Suspension Railway is a suspended funicular located in Dresden, Germany, and connects the districts of Loschwitz and Oberloschwitz. It is one of the oldest suspension railways, having entered service on 6 May 1901, the same year the Wuppertal Schwebebahn entered service.

spots.name: Waldschlösschen Bridge
spots.summary: The Waldschlösschen Bridge is a road bridge across the Elbe river in Dresden. The bridge was intended to remedy inner-city traffic congestion.

spots.name: Mathematisch-Physikalischer Salon
spots.summary: The Mathematisch-Physikalischer Salon in Dresden, Germany, is a museum of historic clocks and scientific instruments.

spots.name: Kupferstich-Kabinett, Dresden
spots.summary: The Kupferstich-Kabinett is part of the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen of Dresden, Germany. Since 2004 it has been located in Dresden Castle.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Dresden Armoury
spots.summary: The Dresden Armoury or Dresden Armory, also known as the Dresden Historical Museum, is one of the world's largest collections of ceremonial weapons, armour and historical textiles. It is part of the Dresden State Art Collections and is located in Dresden Castle in Dresden.

spots.name: Dresden Porcelain Collection
spots.summary: The Dresden Porcelain Collection is part of the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen of Dresden, Germany. It is located in the Zwinger Palace.

spots.name: Schloßplatz
spots.summary: The Schloßplatz is a city square in the center of Dresden, Saxony, Germany. It gets its name from the Dresdner Schloss, the royal residence of the Electors and Kings of Saxony, which faces the south side of the square.

spots.name: Dreikönigskirche
spots.summary: The Dreikönigskirche is a Lutheran church located in the Innere Neustadt of Dresden, Germany. It is the centre of a parish, and a community venue called Haus der Kirche. The church is a listed cultural monument of Dresden.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Japanese Palace
spots.summary: The Japanese Palace is a Baroque building in Dresden, Saxony, Germany. It is located on the Neustadt bank of the river Elbe.

spots.name: New Synagogue
spots.summary: The New Synagogue is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at Hasenberg 1, in the old town of Dresden, Germany. The edifice was completed in 2001 and designed by architects Rena Wandel-Hoefer and Wolfgang Lorch.

spots.name: Johanneum
spots.summary: The Johanneum is a Renaissance building, originally designated as Stallgebäude mit Harnischkammer because it was constructed as the elite part of the electoral mews. It was the first museum of modern times built in 1586-1588 and is located at the Neumarkt in Dresden.

spots.name: Postplatz
spots.summary: The Postplatz is a central square in Dresden and an important traffic junction, especially for local public transport. It is located in the old town not far from the Zwinger.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Dresden Elbe Valley
spots.summary: The Dresden Elbe Valley is a cultural landscape and former World Heritage Site stretching along the Elbe river in Dresden, the state capital of Saxony, Germany.

spots.name: Albrechtsberg Palace
spots.summary: Albrechtsberg Palace or Albrechtsberg Castle is a Neoclassical stately home above the Elbe river in the Loschwitz district of Dresden.

spots.name: Münzkabinett

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Münzkabinett is part of the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden. Founded around 1530, it is one of the oldest museums in Dresden. It is located in Dresden Castle.

spots.name: New Town Hall
spots.summary: The New Town Hall in Dresden is the seat of Dresden's city administration. It is located south-east of the Altmarkt on Dr.-Külz-Ring. The town hall tower is 100.3 metres (329 ft) high ; the viewing platform, which currently is not open to the public, is 68 metres (223 ft) above the ground.

spots.name: Russian Orthodox Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. Simeon of the Wonderful Mountain Church is a Russian Orthodox church in the German city of Dresden. It was designed by Harald Julius von Bosse and Karl Weißbach and built from 1872 to 1874. It is dedicated to Simeon Stylites the Younger.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St. Simeon of the Wonderful Mountain Church

spots.name: Elbwiesen
spots.summary: Go to the (mostly) green river banks, especially on hot summer evenings/nights for a very nice view of the old parts and lot of people playing sports, having barbecues and parties. There are often big concerts and a huge movie screen offers "outdoor cinema."

spots.name: Gläserne Manufaktur
spots.summary: The Transparent Factory previously assembled the electric version of VW's Golf car. Visitors can test drive VW electric cars for 30 minutes (except Sundays). Tours three times a day in English M-Sa, once on Sundays. Until 2016, final assembly for various luxury VW cars took place here.
